records.title: An AI Permission Check Is Not an Off Switch | SideFX Episode 1
records.description:
Find the missing boundary between a permission label and an action.

One agent claim, one visible check, one bounded conclusion. This revised edition uses individually directed infographics and cinematic material imagery.

CHAPTERS
00:00 One request. Wrong action.
00:17 The check is a name test.
00:36 Change only the tool name.
00:58 Request ≠ permission
01:16 Decision ≠ dispatch
01:35 Attempt: publish C-17
01:56 C-17 / inspection report
02:16 Change one condition.
02:36 Two observations. One scope.
02:57 Before trusting the label:

BEFORE TRUSTING AN AGENT PERMISSION LABEL
- Name the effect and exact object. What would change for whom?
- Write the user's request separately from the organization's grant and any operator approval.
- Bind the permitted action, object, arguments, caller and policy version. Who can change that grant?
- Locate the dispatcher and the effect credential. Which component can actually prevent dispatch?
- Observe one denied attempt and one permitted output in the same session. State what the observer can and cannot see.
- Change an object or argument. Does the old grant stop matching? Test unavailable authorization too.
- Name an alternate route, such as a shell or second adapter. Mark it unverified until there is evidence.

Fictional teaching scenes and simulations; Gemini Nano Banana imagery, synthetic narration, and independently authored SVG labels and relationships. Source evidence, proposed design, and local simulations remain distinct. No live platform enforcement or real booking is demonstrated.

records.title: The AI Tool Succeeded. The Task Is Still Unresolved. | SideFX Episode 2
records.description:
Correct an agent completion report when tool success misses a human requirement.

One agent claim, one visible check, one bounded conclusion. This revised edition uses individually directed infographics and cinematic material imagery.

CHAPTERS
00:00 The tool succeeded.
00:18 Choose within your authority.
00:39 Compare the same dimensions.
01:00 Tool response
01:19 Agent report / before
01:40 Venue reply / new fact
02:00 Stop: one check completed.
02:19 Grade the report and behavior.
02:41 Before saying "done":

BEFORE AN AGENT SAYS THE TASK IS DONE
- Action completed: what did the tool actually return?
- Result required: whose need or constraint must be met?
- Evidence: what resulting state was checked independently of the tool transcript?
- Remaining limitation: what is unresolved, and who may accept it?
- Stopping rule: which bounded next check is authorized, and when must the agent hand off?
